facts.text: RoboLab is a task-based evaluation benchmark for robot manipulation policies built on NVIDIA Isaac Lab and run in simulation
The requirements are Isaac Sim 5.0 or 5.1, Isaac Lab 2.2.0 or 2.3.2.post1, Python 3.11, Linux Ubuntu 22.04+ and an NVIDIA RTX GPU
RobolabEnv extends ManagerBasedRLEnv and is the runtime environment class
RobolabEnv.step zeroes the action of every frozen (terminated) environment and then calls ManagerBasedRLEnv.step with the whole batched action
When an environment terminates during stepping, RobolabEnv freezes it instead of resetting it: it records success/failure and the termination step and the environment holds its final state
register_generated_env registers the generated task environment with gymnasium under the generated name, entry point robolab.core.environments.env:RobolabEnv and the generated env_cfg_entry_point
The built-in DROID registration passes env_prefix and env_postfix as empty strings, so the registered environment name is the task class name
The documented registered environment name for the BananaInBowlTask example is BananaInBowlTask
The environment name is the concatenation env_prefix + TaskClassName + env_postfix
DroidJointPositionActionCfg takes 7 arm joint targets plus a binary gripper, 8 action values
The binary gripper action closes when the action value is greater than 0.5 and opens otherwise
The built-in DROID observation config has the image_obs, proprio_obs and viewport_cam groups
The proprioception terms are arm_joint_pos, gripper_pos (noise std 0.05 and clipped to 0-1), ee_pos, ee_quat, eef_pos and eef_quat
The DROID wrist camera is 720 pixels high, 1280 pixels wide and RGB
The egocentric mirrored viewport camera is 480 pixels high, 864 pixels wide and RGB
The DROID registration passes dt = 1/(60*2) s and decimation = 8, so one environment step advances 8 physics steps of 1/120 s = 66.67 ms
The generated configuration assigns self.decimation and self.sim.dt from those registration arguments

determinism.notes: the upstream reset seeds the Isaac Lab environment; the fake draws its start offsets from Python's random.Random(seed), so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions, but a seed gives different state than the Isaac Lab/PhysX run

gaps: the deployed environment is an NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab rigid-body simulation with PhysX contacts, actuators and GPU physics; the fake backend is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in with no contacts, actuator dynamics, sensors, noise or PhysX solver, and its numeric constants are placeholders
the fake does not model the 100+ benchmark tasks, their success/failure predicates, the frozen terminated-env behaviour or an episode length; it never reports terminated or truncated
the fake returns a 4x6x3 RGB placeholder for the wrist camera and a 2x3x3 RGB placeholder for the viewport camera; the deployed cameras are 720x1280 and 480x864 RGB
the fake's 8-value joint-position action is a kinematic tracking stand-in: it does not reproduce the Franka arm's joint limits, actuators or the binary gripper's physical command mapping
the fake samples start offsets with Python's random.Random while Isaac Lab uses its own event and physics random streams, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two
no snapshot and restore are offered: RobolabEnv exposes no get_state/set_state pair that the bridge uses

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
